ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended by Laws No. 78/2003, No. 36/2014, No. 22/2018, and No. 8/2022; Executive Regulations promulgated by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 450/2007, as amended; Law No. 106 of 2013 on Combating Terrorism and Its Financing and its Executive Regulations; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018, together with its Executive Regulations (Ministerial Decree No. 96/1982); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) Board of Directors Decree No. 110 of 2018 concerning the identification and record-keeping of actual beneficiaries in non-banking financial sectors; Central Bank of Egypt customer due diligence rules; and Unified Banking Law No. 194 of 2020.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document of every founding shareholder and natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport or civil records authority of the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961; chain comprising notarization in the country of origin, authentication by the origin country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalization by the competent Egyptian Consulate/Embassy, and final authentication by the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Incumbency where a founding shareholder is a foreign corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry of the foreign shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarial chain through the origin country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the competent Egyptian consulate, and the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs re-authentication office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign corporate shareholder authorizing incorporation of the Egyptian LLC and appointing the local formation agent and authorized counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registrar of the foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarized, sealed, authenticated by the origin country Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and legalized by the Egyptian consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney in favor of the Egyptian formation agent and/or the appointed LLC general manager for incorporation filings and bank signatory mandates
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction; where executed inside Egypt, the Commercial Registry notary (El-Shahr El-Togary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for powers executed outside Egypt; Egyptian notary authentication if executed within Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and recent bank statements of the foreign investor evidencing source of funds for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization of the issuing bank officer's notarized attestation, or authenticated banker's certificate accepted by the beneficiary bank in Egypt

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance / certificate of non-conviction for each natural-person UBO and the local general manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Criminal records authority of the country of residence (Ministry of Interior criminal records department for Egyptian nationals)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization for foreign certificates; direct Ministry of Interior issuance for Egyptian nationals

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law No. 80 of 2002 and EFIU guidance, requiring screening of all founders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and beneficial counterparties against: (i) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, binding on Egypt under its UN Charter obligations and implemented through Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU) circulars; (ii) the national terrorist entities list maintained under Law No. 106 of 2013 by the Egyptian Public Prosecutor; (iii) OFAC SDN and consolidated non-SDN lists, applied as a practical market standard for USD rails, ACH Direct, and correspondent banking de-risking; (iv) Central Bank of Egypt high-risk jurisdiction advisories and MENAFATF public statements; and (v) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions lists where any UBO holds a Western nexus. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including family members and close associates, with senior management approval required before establishment of the business relationship and continuous transaction monitoring thereafter. KYC, UBO, and sanctions screening records must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) 'Invest in Egypt' electronic investor services portal and unified corporate registration platform (https://www.invest-in-egypt.gov.eg), integrated operationally with the Commercial Registry offices of the Ministry of Trade and Industry
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The commercial name must be rendered in Arabic script as the primary statutory denomination; a foreign-language (commonly English) transliteration or companion name may be registered as a secondary denomination, provided the transliteration is phonetically consistent with the Arabic registration. The name must be distinctive, must not describe merely the corporate activity, must not mislead the public as to the corporate objects, may incorporate a personal name only with the named person's written consent, and must terminate with the statutory legal-form marker 'ذات مسؤولية محدودة' or its English abbreviation 'LLC'. GAFI rejects phonetically identical names even where orthography differs and requires the Arabic name to correspond exactly with the authorized foreign transliteration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 'Bank', 'Insurance', 'Reinsurance', 'Takaful', 'Securities', 'Financial', or equivalent terms reserved for institutions licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt or the Financial Regulatory Authority
'Petroleum', 'Oil', 'Gas', 'Pipeline' where sector regulator pre-clearance is not evidenced
'Military', 'Armed Forces', 'National Security', 'State Security', 'Intelligence' (absolute prohibition absent state ownership)
'National', 'Government', 'Ministry', 'Presidential', 'Republic', 'General Authority', 'Municipal' where implied affiliation with the State is objectionable
'Central Bank' and any derivative of 'Central' implying state monetary authority

Religious references including 'Islamic', 'Sharia', 'Quran', 'Christian', 'Coptic', or other faith token requiring administrative religious authority approval and generally declined for commercial platforms
'Arab', 'International', 'Global', 'Egyptian' at the head of the name where the applicant does not demonstrate qualifying pan-regional ownership or standing
'Digital Currency', 'Cryptocurrency', 'Virtual Asset', 'Exchange' attracting heightened EFIU, Central Bank of Egypt, and bank de-risking scrutiny
Names of Egyptian public figures, judges, government office-holders, or identifiable trademarks and famous foreign brands absent documentary trademark consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written refusal from GAFI's Companies Department citing the conflicting or prohibited token. The applicant may: (i) file an administrative objection before GAFI's Complaint and Appeal Committee within 30 calendar days of the refusal, annexing a comparative analysis of conflicting Commercial Registry entries and, where applicable, a written waiver or consent letter from the prior registrant; (ii) where the refusal is grounded on phonetic identity, request a naming-committee adjudication with the Commercial Registry; and (iii) if the administrative appeal is denied or remains undecided within 60 days, file a judicial appeal before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council (Conseil d'État) through a licensed lawyer within 60 days of the adverse decision. In each case the applicant may concurrently reserve an alternative compliant name and proceed with incorporation to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. GAFI and the Commercial Registry require a physical Egyptian address for service of legal notices, court summons, and tax correspondence; a virtual office, digital postbox, or telephony-only address will not satisfy statutory domicile requirements under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976. A serviced or flexible office lease with a dedicated physical suite, a tenancy agreement registered with the relevant Egyptian authorities, and address documentation filed with GAFI constitute the minimum acceptable arrangement for a low-touch SaaS and PropTech entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk of approximately 5-10% over the first three years of operation for a compliant LLC engaged in software services and real estate data SaaS. The Egyptian Tax Authority performs an obligatory fiscal-file visit at incorporation and may conduct unannounced inspections where the registered office is in a residential or shared premise; GAFI and the Commercial Registry verify the registered seat following address amendments; and the onboarding commercial bank for USD rails and ACH correspondent services will normally complete a site verification visit or remote attestation during enhanced due diligence in the first year. Absence of physical substance at the registered office constitutes a material violation under Law No. 159 of 1981 and may ground revocation of the Commercial Registry certificate.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2020), Articles 93-114 (Limited Liability Company regime); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Executive Regulations of Investment Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2017); Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registration Sector (Cairo Investor Service Center and Nafazah digital window).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic incorporation application on Nafazah (single digital entry point) and the certified Arabic Articles of Association, followed by issuance of the Commercial Registration extract and the electronic incorporation certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for LLCs; stated capital is freely determined by the members and must be fully subscribed at formation. Cash subscriptions must be deposited into a dedicated bank escrow account opened in the name of the company under formation, and in-kind contributions must be appraised by a licensed accountant before deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION (written in lieu of meeting) - Unanimously adopted by the founding members and initial directors of the Company. RESOLVED, that the subscription of shares comprising the issued share capital, allocated as set forth in the certified Articles of Association, is approved and accepted. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at the Smart Village office premises, Cairo, Egypt, and the attested lease is adopted as the corporate seat. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Corporate Secretary/Compliance Officer. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to complete the Commercial Registry registration, tax card issuance, social insurance enrollment, and opening of the company bank account, and to take all acts incidental thereto.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Eligibility Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Name Reservation Unit - Egypt Business Center and Nafazah e-portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically three proposed names in Arabic for the LLC 'Proptech Real Estate SaaS' activity. Names must end with 'Sharkat Thaat Masooliya Mahdooda' (LLC) and must not duplicate registered entities, violate public order, or use protected banking and pharmaceutical terms. Pay the nominal reservation fee and obtain the name reservation certificate valid for 12 months.
required_dossiers: Copy of valid national ID or passport of each founding member
Power of attorney if the filing is made through an agent or legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a fresh online application with alternative names immediately after rejection; if the rejection is on legal grounds, file a written objection with the GAFI Legal Affairs Department within 15 days and obtain a reasoned decision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certification of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Notary Public / Syndicate of Commercial Offices in the governorate of the registered office, with GAFI legal pre-review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Arabic Articles of Association ensuring all mandatory LLC provisions are covered: name, object (ISIC 6201 and NAICS 531390 PropTech platform activities), capital and shares, registered office, management, audit appointment, and profit distribution. All members or their authorized attorneys must sign every page; the document is then notarized by the competent commercial-office notary prior to incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Legalized copies of national ID or passport of each shareholder
Minutes of the formation meeting or executed power of attorney
Accountant valuation report if any in-kind contribution is proposed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any legal defect raised by GAFI legal review and re-notarize the corrected pages; no new name reservation is required, but a supplementary annex must be filed with the notary and refiled in the Nafazah application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Capital Escrow Deposit Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed commercial bank in Egypt (Central Bank of Egypt supervision), operating under Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company under formation. Deposit the full subscribed cash capital in Egyptian Pounds. The bank performs customer due diligence and assigns a unique deposit certificate; the certificate must be presented to GAFI and later converted into the permanent corporate bank account upon issuance of the commercial register extract.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID copies and banking reference of each beneficial owner
Written instruction appointing the initial directors as signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank compliance unit requests further beneficial ownership documentation, supply the executed Articles and a shareholder declaration; for non-resident founders, provide legalized passport copy and banking reference; once cleared, request reissuance of the deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing and Legal Review with GAFI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Incorporation and Licensing Sector - Single Window / Nafazah integrated filing system.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the certified Articles, name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and lease contract through the Nafazah application. The GAFI legal examiner confirms that the LLC objects are lawful and that the registered address is compatible with the business scope. Upon validation, GAFI issues the incorporation decision and forwards the file to the Commercial Registry for final registration.
required_dossiers: Attested registered-office lease contract and building permits
Specimen signatures and ID copies of authorized managers
Activity declaration confirming ISIC 6201 / PropTech subscription SaaS model
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the examiner objects to the activity description, file a rectification memorandum narrowing the scope to cloud-based property management software services and re-submit the electronic file; any fee differential is paid and the review is completed within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the competent governorate and the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) local tax office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the CR000 commercial registration form based on the GAFI incorporation decision; the Commercial Registry issues the company's Commercial Registration extract. Simultaneously apply for the ETA tax card and unified tax number; register for payroll withholding and obtain a VAT registration if quarterly taxable supplies exceed the EGP 500,000 threshold. Enroll with the Social Insurance Authority upon hiring employees.
required_dossiers: Attested lease contract and electricity bill for the registered office
Copy of the incorporation certificate and IDs of all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA delays the tax card or challenges the activity code, file a service request through the ETA electronic window, attach the GAFI certificate, and request re-classification under ISIC 6201; any VAT registration issue is cured by written confirmation of the commencement of taxable supplies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Competent district municipality (e.g. New Cairo District) and the Civil Defense Department of the Ministry of Interior.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply to the district for the annual commercial/professional operating license covering a software services office. The civil defense inspection verifies fire safety equipment, alarms, emergency exits, and structural load clearance for the office floor. The insurance certificate is presented, and the final operating license is posted in the office.
required_dossiers: Insurance policy for fire and public liability
Occupational health and safety checklist for the IT workplace
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the district commissioner returns the application for deficiencies, remedy the technical notes (installed fire extinguishers, exit signage) and resubmit; persistent delay may be escalated to the governorate technical office for a final decision within 10 working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 6201 (software programming and cloud SaaS) is not an industrial activity under Industrial Licensing Law No. 15 of 2017; the company may voluntarily register with the Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA) for digital export facilitation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Commercial/Professional Operating License (Rukhsat Tashghil) issued by the district authority; no manufacturing operating license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office and information technology services are not listed in the EIA screening annexes (Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended by Law No. 9 of 2009, Ministerial Decree No. 249 of 1996); no EIA technical report or registration certificate is mandated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC point sources apply. General compliance is required with Law No. 4 of 1994 ambient air quality limit values if a diesel back-up generator is installed; e-waste (servers, batteries, electrical equipment) must be handled through authorized recyclers under Waste Management Law No. 202 of 2020; sanitary wastewater is discharged to the public sewer in accordance with Law No. 93 of 1962.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil protection clearance under Law No. 12 of 2018 covers fire extinguisher sufficiency, smoke alarms, emergency exit marking, and evacuation drills; a structural load inspection letter is obtained for the leased office floor to confirm suitability for installed server and telecom racks; occupational health and safety clearance under the workplaces chapter of Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 is required before full staffing, together with workers' compensation insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); official e-portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must register via the ETA online portal, submitting certified constitutional documents (articles of association, commercial registration), a power of attorney, and, where required, appointment of a local tax representative. Upon approval, the ETA issues a unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) covering both income tax and VAT obligations. Non-residents may complete remote electronic registration; notarized documentation must be uploaded for biometric verification waiver.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election exists under Egyptian law. The LLC is mandatorily taxed as a separate corporate person; the only available election is the fiscal year-end (calendar or non-calendar). Limited investment incentives require formal ETA/investment approval but do not alter core tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover for mandatory VAT registration; no threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of electronic services; voluntary registration is permitted below threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Egypt mandates a real-time e-invoicing clearance system for B2B transactions. VAT-registered taxpayers must integrate their billing/ERP system with the ETA via API, submit invoices in the approved XML scheme, obtain a digital approval code, and include a QR code on each invoice. The system is enforced in phases; failure to obtain real-time clearance can invalidate the invoice and trigger penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated if the goods physically leave Egypt and are supported by customs proof. Services supplied to non-residents qualify for zero-rating where the service is rendered and consumed wholly outside Egypt, as evidenced by the commercial agreement, hosting infrastructure location, and absence of any Egyptian resident beneficiary. For PropTech/SaaS, the software must be delivered via cloud infrastructure outside Egypt; advertising or support services delivered to Egyptian residents may disallow zero-rating.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims are subject to periodic ETA audit. If the export documentation is incomplete, FX is not repatriated within 180 days, or a zero-rated supply is later found to be taxable, the ETA may assess the uncollected VAT plus late-payment interest and fines of up to 100% of the tax. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger administrative clawback of refunded amounts and may lead to criminal prosecution and debarment from the e-invoicing clearance system.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) acting as the sole monetary authority, bank regulator, and foreign-exchange administrator under Law No. 194 of 2020 (the Central Bank and Banking System Law). The CBE's Foreign Exchange Operations Department, together with the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) and the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), supervises currency convertibility, capital-import verification, and profit repatriation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and, after the March 2024 exchange-rate reform, operates a unified, market-determined exchange rate. Current-account transactions (SaaS export receipts, subscription fees, software royalties, and operational payments) are freely convertible and transferable through authorised banks. Capital-account transactions (inbound equity, shareholder loans, and outward profit remittances) are convertible only after bank validation of the underlying investment (GAFI certificate and CBE capital-account registration), confirmation of the source of funds of the original inward remittance, and clearance of Egyptian corporate tax and payroll obligations. Profit remittance hurdles are practical rather than statutory: banks prioritise FX liquidity, may require a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority, and reject repatriation if the USD/EUR trail does not trace back to the registered capital injection. For a PropTech SaaS exporter, the bulk of revenue will arrive as Stripe/ACH settlements in USD; these must be swept into the Egyptian banking system and matched to the export contract to avoid classification as informal FX circulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign-exchange instructions implementing Law No. 194 of 2020, all export proceeds for goods and services must be repatriated through the licensed Egyptian banking system: the statutory timeline is 120 days from the bill of lading for goods and 90 days from invoice/service delivery for services, with a six-month extension available upon prior CBE justification. Mandatory conversion ratios are imposed by CBE prudential directive rather than by statute; for service-export receipts (including ISIC 6201 SaaS and cloud-platform licences) the current floor is 0% forced conversion, meaning the LLC may retain, borrow against, or convert its USD receivables at the prevailing market rate, provided 100% of the proceeds pass through the Egyptian bank and are supported by the export contract, digital-delivery evidence, and the CBE transaction declaration. Goods exporters remain subject to a possible CBE-imposed conversion floor (set at 50% during recent external-liquidity stress), but that floor does not apply to software subscription receivables. Late repatriation is an exchange-control violation under Article 20 of Law No. 194 of 2020 and may result in fines, bank-level restrictions, and a compliance flag affecting future treasury operations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Account + USD Capital Repatriation Account
EGP Operational Account + Multi-Currency Revenue Account
EGP Operational Account + USD/EUR Clearing and Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: EGP Operational Account + Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary or principal treasury rail; MEDIUM as a supplementary offshore collection node. Non-bank fintech EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are not CBE-licensed deposit takers and cannot lawfully hold EGP or provide local current-account services in Egypt. They may be used only to collect USD/EUR/GBP SaaS receivables from Stripe Billing and ACH Direct before automatic sweeping into a licensed Egyptian bank account; the Egyptian LLC must not use the EMI as its bank of record or settle local payroll/tax obligations from the EMI balance. The Payment Systems Law No. 18 of 2019 requires all EGP-denominated payment services and clearing to be routed through CBE-authorized banks/SWIFT channels. The viable structure is therefore: Stripe/ACH -> EMI or correspondent USD account -> MT103/MT940 sweep to CIB/NBE -> EGP conversion (if needed) at the CBE market rate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is not uniformly available. Tier-1 Egyptian banks require at least one physical account-opening interview for a non-resident-owned LLC. The CBE's digital KYC framework permits video verification, but domestic market practice is a physical appearance by the legal representative or a resident general manager holding a notarised and consular-legalised power of attorney; the ultimate beneficial owner may attend remotely in most banks but is subject to a sanctions/PEP screening. A pure paper-only onboarding is possible only through a documented existing banking relationship or a direct corporate-credit endorsement, and is generally Low viability for a newly formed PropTech LLC. This should be scheduled 4-6 weeks before treasury go-live to accommodate apostille/legalisation delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face SaaS revenue pattern with thousands of micro-transactions is characterised as layering or unlicensed money-service activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe merchant account agreement and settlement statements; export service contracts; order-to-cash reconciliation ledger mapping each settlement run to the Egyptian accounting records; and a written treasury policy confirming 100% routing to the licensed Egyptian bank and a ban on P2P/cash-conversion channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder injecting initial capital with historical or opaque source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled incorporation documents of the shareholder, MT103 remittance records of the inbound transfers, audited financial statements or bank statements evidencing accumulation of funds, the completed CBE capital-account form, and the GAFI Investment Certificate naming the Egyptian LLC as beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction footprint of UBO or operation of multiple offshore SaaS/holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO identity, tax-residency and PEP status certificate; OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening results; group structure chart; contractor due-diligence file with valid IDs and invoices; and a declaration confirming no sanctioned counterparty or direct offshore EGP settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Administrative blocker: repeated rejection of inbound equity transfer due to incorrect reference/purpose code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-verified SWIFT MT103 template using ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity) or 'LOAN' (intercompany loan); bank-issued foreign-exchange declaration forms pre-approved by the compliance unit; and a written CBE correspondence log evidencing that the rejection was solely a code-matter and not substantive AML.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the LLC's licensed Egyptian bank using the exact beneficiary name/BIC/IBAN registered in the CBE capital-account file. The bank opens the inward investment file upon presentation of: (i) GAFI investment registration; (ii) the CBE capital-account declaration; (iii) a shareholder resolution approving the capital increase and share issuance; and (iv) AML clearance evidencing the remitter's source of funds. The remittance must be tagged with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' for equity or 'LOAN' for shareholder/subordinated loan, and the reference line must quote the GAFI registration number and the Egyptian entity ID. The bank will credit the USD capital account, issue a foreign-currency deposit receipt, and report the inflow under the CBE balance-of-payments reporting file, thereby enabling later profit repatriation. A completed inward capital file is mandatory; without it, a profit/dividend remittance will be administratively blocked.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements (AWS/cloud fees, international software licences, overseas contractors) are executed through the Egyptian bank's SWIFT MT103 module from the USD/EUR revenue account after submission of the underlying contract, invoice, and a current-account foreign-exchange declaration; no documentary ceiling applies for genuine SaaS operational payments, provided the transaction value matches the commercial agreement. The bank settles via its correspondent network (typically Citibank, JPMorgan, or Standard Chartered) in USD, EUR, or GBP through CHIPS/Fedwire or TARGET2. For on-prem hardware or infrastructure procurement requiring bank undertaking, an irrevocable sight commercial letter of credit is available at NBE/CIB; for digital SaaS delivery, an LC is not advised because the absence of transport documents creates discrepancy risk. Inbound Stripe/ACH USD settlements are received through the same correspondent chain and manually matched to the Stripe payout report; daily liquidity should be managed with a zero-balance sweep between the USD revenue account and EGP payroll/tax account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable USD/EGP FX forwards up to 12 months with CBE-authorised domestic banks, strictly backed by the underlying SaaS export exposure
OTC vanilla EUR/USD and USD/GBP currency options used to hedge a multi-currency subscriber-revenue base, subject to bank counterparty credit approval and CBE non-speculation attestation
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) on a foreign-currency shareholder loan or project finance facility, matching the maturity and cash flows of the financial liability
Trade-backed forward foreign exchange covering the invoice-to-bank-settlement lag of Stripe/ACH receivables, with payment direction made upon the bank's receipt of the underlying export documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 19) with audited financial statements, transfer pricing disclosure form, and tax reconciliation schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Corporate Income Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; April 30 for calendar-year taxpayers; alternate fiscal year requires ETA pre-approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment penalty of 2% per month on unpaid tax, late-filing fine of EGP 1,000-5,000 plus EGP 500 per month, and estimated assessment by ETA; absence of tax clearance blocks annual Commercial Registry renewal, and prolonged non-compliance triggers administrative strike-off within 12 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of Commercial Registration Certificate and payment of GAFI services fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office, Ministry of Trade and Industry (GAFI one-stop shop)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days preceding the registration anniversary date; calendar billing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal penalty of EGP 200-1,000 plus accumulated arrears; registration card suspended after 6 months of non-renewal; commercial registration entry administratively struck off after 12 months, triggering company dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting approval of audited financial statements, profit appropriation, and auditor re-appointment; filing of approved statements and resolutions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (post-meeting filing) and Egyptian Tax Authority (attachment to Form No. 19)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: OGM within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by June 30 for calendar-year taxpayers); approved statements and resolutions filed within 15 days after the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 1,000-3,000 per violation under Law 159/1981, Article 152; failure to hold the OGM or file approved statements blocks annual Commercial Registry renewal and constitutes a statutory ground for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Real Beneficiary (UBO) register annual validation and GAFI disclosure update including shareholding changes and senior-management confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days of any ownership or control change; mandatory re-validation at each annual Commercial Registry renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EGP 10,000-100,000 for material omission or false UBO statement under Law 4/2022; renewal refusal until full compliance; personal criminal liability of the LLC manager; persistent non-compliance leads to administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Mandatory annual subscription to the Egyptian Chamber of Commerce (membership contribution)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federation of Egyptian Chambers of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the annual Commercial Registry renewal; calendar-year billing cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears prevent issuance of the annual commercial registration card and certificates of origin; prolonged non-payment suspends Commercial Registry renewal and contributes to administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every Egyptian LLC without turnover exemption: a licensed independent auditor must be appointed at the OGM, audited financial statements must accompany the CIT return, and audited statements must be presented to shareholders. Companies preparing simplified tax-basis statements under Law 30/2023 (revenue up to EGP 20 million) still require auditor attestation for CIT filing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by Decree 110/2015 and IFRS-converged; entities with revenue above EGP 20 million apply full IFRS-converged EAS, while smaller entities may apply the simplified small-entity framework under the EAS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a Real Beneficiary (UBO) register identifying every ultimate owner or controlling person as defined under Law 4/2022, with ownership percentages, voting control, and indirect interests. The register is filed with GAFI at incorporation, updated within 15 days of any share transfer or control change, and re-validated against the shareholder ledger and share-transfer log at each annual Commercial Registry renewal. The resident manager must sign the annual UBO confirmation statement; a false or omitted declaration is a criminal offense under Law 4/2022.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholder ledger with ownership percentages and transfer records)
Minute Book (shareholders' resolutions and manager resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,500 per year (virtual office with legal address, mail handling, and local correspondence; no statutory registered-agent nominee requirement for Egyptian LLCs)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 - 2,500 per year (SME audit fee in Cairo for a low-volume PropTech SaaS LLC with cloud ordering and ACH billing)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly established SMEs under Law 152/2020 may elect a reduced tax rate based on annual turnover, with effective rates from 0.5% to 2.5% for turnover up to approximately EGP 20 million; qualified exporters in Free Zones and the Suez Canal Economic Zone may obtain exemption from corporate income tax and customs duties; Investment Law No. 72/2017 provides capital-based tax deductions (up to 50% of investment cost) for eligible projects in targeted regions or labor-intensive industries. All incentives require prior ETA registration and do not apply automatically to a PropTech SaaS entity without factual qualifying activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified e-tax portal; Corporate Income Tax Return Form No. 2 for legal persons, accompanied by the TP declaration, audited financial statements, and supporting schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly provisional CIT advance payments are required during the year, with the annual Form No. 2 due within four months after fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year Egyptian LLC, the final return and payment are due no later than 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax card number, commercial registration number, fiscal year-end, legal form, registered address, and authorized representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC must quote its Egyptian tax/EIN, PE notification file, and commercial registration; the non-resident parent must be identified as controlling shareholder and local manager as agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross receipts from PropTech subscriptions, property-screening software fees, tenant-screening reports, Stripe/ACH settlement amounts, and real-estate management ancillary fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egyptian-source revenue attributable to the Egyptian branch or LLC; exclude foreign services performed outside Egypt, but maintain an arm's-length revenue allocation model.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Cost of Sales and Operating Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cloud infrastructure, software maintenance, data licensing, marketing, professional fees, personnel, rent, and office costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses incurred for the Egyptian activity with proper VAT/tax invoices; head-office allocated charges are allowed only under Article 32 and must be supported by a TP policy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of office and computer equipment, fixtures, and amortization of capitalized SaaS platform development costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fixed assets physically used in Egypt are depreciated per ETA schedules; imported used assets require customs documentation and written independent valuation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of parent guarantees, intercompany royalties, management fees, technology access fees, centralized cloud services, and cross-border subscription routing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Egyptian Local File, Master File, CbCR notification, and TP declaration as applicable; non-disclosure, even below documentation thresholds, is separately punishable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 16 - DTA and Foreign Tax Credit Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for tax treaty benefits, relief at source on dividends/interest/royalties, and foreign withholding tax credits on cross-border receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit tax residency certificate (TRC), beneficial ownership declaration, source-country WHT certificates, and legalization/apostille documents before final assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers additional tax of 2% per month or part thereof on unpaid tax, subject to a minimum fixed fine of EGP 1,000 and an administrative fine up to EGP 20,000. Late payment after final assessment adds up to 100% of the unpaid tax, asset attachment, suspension of tax clearance, and travel-ban measures.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Monthly provisional CIT advance payment declaration submitted through the ETA e-tax portal; reconciled with annual Form No. 2.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Monthly advance CIT payment is due by the end of the month following the month for which profits are estimated. Newly established companies may pay based on estimated current-year profits and reconcile at annual filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration month, tax card number, and unique entity identifier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Egyptian LLC or PE tax card code; never file under the foreign parent's tax reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Provisional Taxable Profit and Advance Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimated cumulative taxable profit, computed 22.5% CIT, less previous installments and WHT credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use actual Egyptian-source revenue and deductible costs to date for the estimate; retain reconciliations to avoid under-withholding penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Non-payment of monthly advance installments incurs 2% monthly late-payment tax, with a minimum fine of EGP 1,000; repeated non-compliance may block the entity's e-tax account and customs/import permits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on gross cash dividends remitted to non-resident shareholders under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, unless a double-tax treaty reduces the rate or a domestic exemption applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must submit to the ETA: (i) a tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority for the relevant period, generally legalized or apostilled; (ii) a beneficial ownership declaration confirming no pass-through arrangement; (iii) ownership and shareholding-period evidence; and (iv) a written request for reduced withholding or exemption before the distribution/remittance date. The ETA may issue an advance lower-withholding certificate or refund excess WHT after final assessment. Documents must be retained for at least five years and ownership changes reported to the ETA within 30 days.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: interest paid to non-residents is subject to 20% WHT; royalties, including software, patent, trademark, and know-how license payments, are subject to 20% gross-basis WHT. Under most Egyptian DTAs, the treaty rate for royalties and interest ranges from 10% to 15% depending on the instrument and ownership; reduced treaty rates require the same TRC and beneficial-ownership proof. For PropTech SaaS, recurring subscription fees are service income only if the customer does not obtain permanent possession or access to the underlying software IP; perpetual licenses, source-code access, and data-IP licensing are generally royalty payments subject to WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Egyptian Local File is required when the aggregate value of controlled transactions in a fiscal year exceeds EGP 6,000,000, or where annual business revenues exceed EGP 20,000,000. Master File and CbC report notification are required for multinational groups with consolidated global revenue above EGP 7,000,000,000. A transfer-pricing declaration is mandatory on the corporate income tax return even where documentation thresholds are not crossed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime similar to UAE offshore centers. However, Article 32 of Income Tax Law No. 91/2005 embodies substance-over-form: the ETA may disregard artificial or sham transactions and recharacterize arrangements lacking commercial rationale. In treaty-relief cases, the beneficial-ownership test prevents shell holding companies from accessing lower dividend, interest, or royalty withholding rates. A PropTech LLC that is a nominal tombstone company without personnel, management premises, active board conduct, or substantive platform activity will fail anti-abuse and TP review.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false Form No. 2, omitting Stripe/ACH subscription revenue, issuing forged property-service invoices, destroying accounting records, or intentionally understating recurring SaaS income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion penalty of 100% of avoided tax, 2% monthly late-payment interest, administrative fine up to EGP 200,000, and imprisonment of 2 to 5 years; ETA may additionally impose a 30% concealment addition where accounts have been falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories who signed or caused the false return are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; ETA may issue a travel ban, seize personal assets, disqualify the director, and pursue criminal imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse / Synthetic Margin Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing extreme intercompany royalties, centralized management fees, or inflated cloud/data fees that leave no arm's-length profit in the Egyptian LLC; failing to prepare Local File, TP policy, or benchmark study; circular fund flows between the PropTech platform and foreign affiliate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA applies a transfer-pricing adjustment disallowing the non-arm's-length expense, adds 100% of the corrected income, imposes penalty up to 25% of the adjustment, and accrues 2% monthly interest for non-disclosure; failure to maintain TP documentation brings fixed penalties up to EGP 150,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving such arrangements without substance face a personal tax assessment for unpaid CIT attributable to the pricing adjustment, administrative penalties on the underpaid tax, and cross-border enforcement through asset freezing and travel restriction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an offshore holding company without real economic activity solely to claim lower dividend WHT under a DTA while the LLC distributes substantially all profits annually.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA denies the DTA benefit, imposes the full 10% statutory dividend WHT, adds a penalty of up to 100% of the under-withheld tax, 2% monthly late-payment interest, and may block further dividend remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for unremitted WHT on distributions; failure to withhold and remit is a criminal default carrying personal fines, travel bans, and imprisonment of up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LLC as a conduit for undisclosed beneficial owners, layering payments through unrelated PropTech entities, creating fictitious ACH customers to justify cash receipts, or accepting real-estate deposits without legitimate platform service.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002 and counterterrorist financing amendments: imprisonment of 3 to 7 years, fines of EGP 100,000 to EGP 10,000,000, confiscation of funds and property, and suspension of licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge or willful blindness bear joint and several criminal liability; personal assets are frozen, travel bans issued, restitution of laundered amounts required, and imprisonment to seven years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold on Royalties and Interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying offshore software/data licensing fees or intra-group interest to non-residents without applying the 20% statutory WHT and without an ETA-approved treaty reduction certificate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA grosses up the underlying payment, assesses the unpaid WHT against the Egyptian LLC, imposes a 100% non-withholding penalty, adds 2% monthly late-payment interest, and disallows the underlying expense as non-deductible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who control payments are personally liable for the unremitted WHT and cannot escape liability through liquidation; ETA may freeze the operating bank account and issue personal travel bans until the WHT is fully settled.
